# Step 8: Elephant damage

Recent elephant damage should be found only where elephants live. Each report of elephant damage is compared with the ranges of the savanna elephant (*Loxodonta africana*) and the forest elephant (*L. cyclotis*) in the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, including areas where either species is probably or possibly extant, because West African sites may fall in either range. A report more than `r elephant_range_buffer_km` km from both ranges is left empty and flagged; the rest of the record is kept. The range polygons are read from a local copy and are never deposited, because the IUCN terms do not allow redistribution.

```{r}
#| label: elephant-checks

# The evidence that a record is a tree (Step 10) uses the answers as recorded,
# before this check empties any of them.
tree_evidence_values <- working_data[tree_evidence_variables]

# first_value_of() returns the distinct values of the first of the named
# fields that a table has, joined by "; ", or "" if it has none of them.
first_value_of <- function(table, field_names) {
  field <- intersect(field_names, names(table))[1]
  if (is.na(field)) return("")
  paste(sort(unique(na.omit(as.character(table[[field]])))), collapse = "; ")
}

# read_elephant_range() reads the range polygons of the listed species from
# every GeoPackage or shapefile in a folder, whether the species come in one
# file or one file per species. The species column is "sci_name" in recent
# IUCN downloads and "binomial" in older ones. It returns the repaired
# polygons and a table of what was read from each file, and stops if any
# listed species has no polygons.
read_elephant_range <- function(folder) {
  files <- list.files(folder, pattern = "\\.(gpkg|shp)$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
  if (length(files) == 0) stop("No GeoPackage or shapefile was found in ", folder, call. = FALSE)
  pieces  <- list()
  sources <- list()
  for (file in files) {
    for (layer in sf::st_layers(file)$name) {
      fields <- names(sf::st_read(file, query = sprintf('SELECT * FROM "%s" WHERE FID < 0', layer), quiet = TRUE))
      species_field  <- intersect(c("sci_name", "SCI_NAME", "binomial", "BINOMIAL"), fields)[1]
      presence_field <- intersect(c("presence", "PRESENCE"), fields)[1]
      if (is.na(species_field)) next
      species_list <- paste0("'", elephant_species, "'", collapse = ", ")
      piece <- sf::st_read(file, query = sprintf('SELECT * FROM "%s" WHERE "%s" IN (%s)', layer, species_field,
                                                 species_list), quiet = TRUE)
      if (nrow(piece) == 0) next
      if (!is.na(presence_field)) piece <- piece[as_number(piece[[presence_field]]) %in% elephant_presence_codes, ]
      if (nrow(piece) == 0) next
      # One row per species and file: what was kept, and the IUCN fields
      # that identify the assessment, for citing the data.
      for (species in intersect(elephant_species, unique(piece[[species_field]]))) {
        rows <- piece[piece[[species_field]] == species, ]
        sources[[length(sources) + 1]] <- tibble(
          species = species, file = basename(file), layer = layer, polygons = nrow(rows),
          presence_codes_kept = if (is.na(presence_field)) "no presence field" else
            paste(sort(unique(as_number(rows[[presence_field]]))), collapse = ", "),
          year_compiled = first_value_of(rows, c("yrcompiled", "YRCOMPILED")),
          citation = first_value_of(rows, c("citation", "CITATION")))
      }
      pieces[[length(pieces) + 1]] <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_geometry(piece), 4326)
    }
  }
  sources <- bind_rows(sources)
  missing_species <- setdiff(elephant_species, sources$species)
  if (length(missing_species) > 0) {
    stop("No range polygons of ", paste(missing_species, collapse = " or "), " were found in ", folder,
         ". Download the IUCN Red List range data of every species in elephant_species.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  # Polygons are repaired with GEOS in the projected system, because the
  # spherical engine (s2) refuses loops whose edges cross.
  previous_s2 <- sf_use_s2(FALSE)
  on.exit(suppressMessages(sf_use_s2(previous_s2)), add = TRUE)
  ranges <- sf::st_transform(do.call(c, pieces), elephant_check_crs)
  ranges <- sf::st_make_valid(ranges)
  ranges <- ranges[!sf::st_is_empty(ranges)]
  ranges <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_collection_extract(ranges, "POLYGON"))
  if (length(ranges) == 0) stop("The elephant range polygons could not be repaired.", call. = FALSE)
  list(ranges = ranges, sources = sources)
}

# near_elephant_range() tells, for each point, whether it lies within the
# buffer distance of a range polygon. It measures on the sphere (s2); if s2
# refuses a repaired polygon, it measures in the projected system instead.
near_elephant_range <- function(points, ranges, distance_m) {
  previous_s2 <- sf_use_s2(TRUE)
  on.exit(suppressMessages(sf_use_s2(previous_s2)), add = TRUE)
  spherical <- tryCatch({
    ranges_lonlat <- sf::st_transform(ranges, 4326)
    lengths(sf::st_is_within_distance(sf::st_transform(points, 4326), ranges_lonlat, dist = distance_m)) > 0
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(spherical)) return(list(near = spherical, method = "on the sphere"))
  suppressMessages(sf_use_s2(FALSE))
  planar <- lengths(sf::st_is_within_distance(sf::st_transform(points, elephant_check_crs), ranges,
                                              dist = distance_m)) > 0
  list(near = planar, method = "in an azimuthal equidistant projection centred on Africa")
}

elephant_check_run <- FALSE
elephant_distance_method <- NA_character_
elephant_range_sources <- tibble()
elephant_damage_outside_range <- rep(FALSE, number_of_records)
if (!is.na(elephant_variable)) {
  damage_answer   <- working_data[[elephant_variable]]
  damage_tidy     <- str_squish(str_replace_all(tolower(coalesce(damage_answer, "")), "[^a-z0-9 ]", " "))
  damage_reported <- is_filled(damage_answer) & !damage_tidy %in% no_damage_answers
  folder_found    <- is_filled(elephant_range_folder) && dir.exists(elephant_range_folder)

  # The check is required unless require_elephant_check is FALSE: a missing
  # folder or Red List version stops the document here.
  if (require_elephant_check && !folder_found) {
    stop("The elephant range folder was not found (", elephant_range_folder, "). Set elephant_range_folder in ",
         "1_Harmonise_tree_data.R, or set require_elephant_check to FALSE for a test run.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (require_elephant_check && !is_filled(iucn_red_list_version)) {
    stop("Set iucn_red_list_version in 1_Harmonise_tree_data.R: the Red List version must be cited. ",
         "Set require_elephant_check to FALSE for a test run.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  # The ranges must never be deposited, so they must not sit in the folder
  # of the public file.
  if (folder_found && startsWith(normalizePath(elephant_range_folder, winslash = "/"),
                                 normalizePath(public_data_folder, winslash = "/"))) {
    stop("The elephant range folder is inside the public data folder, which is deposited. Move it.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (folder_found) {
    elephant_range_read    <- read_elephant_range(elephant_range_folder)
    elephant_range         <- elephant_range_read$ranges
    elephant_range_sources <- elephant_range_read$sources
    # Internal record of the ranges used, for citing them; never published.
    write_excel_csv(elephant_range_sources, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "elephant_range_sources.csv"),
                    na = "")
    distance_test <- near_elephant_range(record_points, elephant_range, elephant_range_buffer_km * 1000)
    elephant_distance_method <- distance_test$method
    near_range <- rep(NA, number_of_records)
    near_range[record_points$record_number] <- distance_test$near
    elephant_damage_outside_range <- damage_reported & near_range %in% FALSE
    record_issues("elephant damage", which(elephant_damage_outside_range), elephant_variable,
                  damage_answer[elephant_damage_outside_range],
                  paste("elephant damage reported more than", elephant_range_buffer_km,
                        "km from the IUCN elephant ranges"), "error", "value left empty")
    working_data[[elephant_variable]][elephant_damage_outside_range] <- NA
    elephant_check_run <- TRUE
  } else {
    print_to_console("\nThe elephant range folder was not found (", elephant_range_folder,
                     "); the elephant damage check was not run (require_elephant_check is FALSE).")
  }
}
```

`r if (elephant_check_run) paste0("The ranges were read from ", nrow(elephant_range_sources), " file and species combination", if (nrow(elephant_range_sources) != 1) "s" else "", " (", paste0("*", elephant_range_sources$species, "*: ", format(elephant_range_sources$polygons, big.mark = ","), " polygon", ifelse(elephant_range_sources$polygons == 1, "", "s"), " from ", elephant_range_sources$file, collapse = "; "), "; details in elephant_range_sources.csv). Distances were measured ", elephant_distance_method, ". Elephant damage was reported in ", format(sum(damage_reported), big.mark = ","), " records; ", format(sum(elephant_damage_outside_range), big.mark = ","), " of these lay more than ", elephant_range_buffer_km, " km from both ranges and the value was left empty (IUCN Red List version ", if (is_filled(iucn_red_list_version)) iucn_red_list_version else "not recorded", ").") else "**The elephant damage check was not run, because the IUCN range data were not found and require_elephant_check is FALSE. This run must not be used for the public file.**"`

# Step 9: Species names

Species names are first corrected using the list of known misspellings (`species_name_corrections.csv`), and then matched to the World Flora Online (WFO) taxonomic backbone with the `WorldFlora` package. The accepted name is added in `accepted_species_name`, only where the match is at species level or below. The public file carries `accepted_species_name` only: the name as recorded (`species_name`) is used for matching and kept in the internal reports, and the other taxonomy columns (`taxonomic_status`, `family`, `wfo_taxon_id`) are used for review only and are not published. Only exact matches are accepted. Approximate (fuzzy) matches can point to the wrong species, so they are not accepted automatically; they are listed with the suggested name, and a suggestion is accepted by adding it to the corrections list. Records of `r paste0('*', sensitive_species, '*', collapse = ', ')`, a species at risk of illegal harvesting, are removed from the public file together with their photographs (Step 10), because a position or a photograph would expose the tree; the species is listed in the manuscript.

```{r}
#| label: species-names

species_corrections <- tibble(species_name = character(), corrected_species_name = character())
if (is_filled(input_paths$species_corrections_file) && file.exists(input_paths$species_corrections_file)) {
  species_corrections <- read_as_text(input_paths$species_corrections_file)
  names(species_corrections) <- to_dictionary_style(names(species_corrections))
  if (!all(c("species_name", "corrected_species_name") %in% names(species_corrections))) {
    stop("The species corrections file needs the columns species_name and corrected_species_name.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
}

# A correction to an empty name marks the recorded name as unidentifiable.
recorded_species <- working_data[[species_variable]]
correction_index <- match(tolower(recorded_species), tolower(str_squish(species_corrections$species_name)))
name_for_matching <- recorded_species
corrected <- !is.na(correction_index)
name_for_matching[corrected] <- species_corrections$corrected_species_name[correction_index[corrected]]
name_for_matching[!is_filled(name_for_matching)] <- NA
record_issues("species names", which(corrected), species_variable, recorded_species[corrected],
              "name in the corrections list", "note", "corrected name used for matching")

taxonomy_columns <- c("accepted_species_name", "taxonomic_status", "family", "wfo_taxon_id")
for (column in taxonomy_columns) working_data[[column]] <- NA_character_
species_review <- tibble()

# find_wfo_backbone_file() accepts the backbone file or the folder that holds
# it.
find_wfo_backbone_file <- function(path) {
  if (!dir.exists(path)) return(path)
  candidates <- list.files(path, pattern = "^classification\\.(csv|txt)$", ignore.case = TRUE,
                           recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(candidates) == 0) {
    zipped <- list.files(path, pattern = "\\.zip$", ignore.case = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
    stop("No WFO backbone file (classification.csv or classification.txt) was found in the folder ",
         path, ".",
         if (length(zipped) > 0) paste0(" The folder holds ", paste(zipped, collapse = ", "),
                                        ": please unzip it first.") else "",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (length(candidates) > 1) {
    message("Several WFO backbone files were found; using ", candidates[1])
  }
  candidates[1]
}

wfo_backbone_available <- is_filled(input_paths$wfo_backbone_file) && file.exists(input_paths$wfo_backbone_file)
if (wfo_backbone_available) {
  input_paths$wfo_backbone_file <- find_wfo_backbone_file(input_paths$wfo_backbone_file)
}

if (wfo_backbone_available) {
  for (package in c("WorldFlora", "data.table")) {
    if (!requireNamespace(package, quietly = TRUE)) stop("Please install the package ", package, " to match species names.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  # The column check reports a wrong WFO download clearly.
  wfo_backbone <- data.table::fread(input_paths$wfo_backbone_file, encoding = "UTF-8")
  needed_wfo_columns <- c("taxonID", "scientificName", "taxonRank", "taxonomicStatus", "family")
  missing_wfo_columns <- setdiff(needed_wfo_columns, names(wfo_backbone))
  if (length(missing_wfo_columns) > 0) {
    stop("The WFO backbone file ", input_paths$wfo_backbone_file, " lacks the columns: ",
         paste(missing_wfo_columns, collapse = ", "),
         ". Use classification.csv from the WFO taxonomic backbone (DwC) download.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  # Names are cleaned as WorldFlora::WFO.match() cleans them before matching.
  worldflora_qualifiers <- eval(formals(WorldFlora::WFO.match)$sub.pattern)
  clean_name_like_worldflora <- function(names) {
    cleaned <- str_squish(names)
    for (qualifier in worldflora_qualifiers) cleaned <- gsub(qualifier, "", cleaned)
    cleaned <- str_squish(str_remove(cleaned, "\\(.*$"))
    has_number <- str_detect(cleaned, "[[:digit:]]")
    cleaned[has_number] <- str_remove(word(cleaned[has_number], 1), "[[:digit:]]+$")
    cleaned
  }

  # can_be_matched() excludes very short names, which stop WorldFlora 1.14-5
  # with an error.
  can_be_matched <- function(names) {
    nchar(coalesce(word(clean_name_like_worldflora(names), 1), "")) > 2
  }

  distinct_names    <- sort(unique(na.omit(name_for_matching)))
  unmatchable_names <- distinct_names[!can_be_matched(distinct_names)]
  names_to_match    <- setdiff(distinct_names, unmatchable_names)
  if (length(unmatchable_names) > 0) {
    message("Species names not submitted to WorldFlora (not recognisable scientific names): ",
            paste(unmatchable_names, collapse = "; "))
  }

  wfo_best <- data.frame()
  if (length(names_to_match) > 0) {
    wfo_candidates <- tryCatch(
      suppressMessages(WorldFlora::WFO.match(
        spec.data = data.frame(spec.name = names_to_match, input_name = names_to_match),
        WFO.data = wfo_backbone, verbose = FALSE)),
      error = function(e) {
        stop("WorldFlora::WFO.match() failed: ", conditionMessage(e),
             ". A species name may need adding to species_name_corrections.csv.", call. = FALSE)
      })
    wfo_best <- suppressMessages(WorldFlora::WFO.one(wfo_candidates, verbose = FALSE))
  }

  take_wfo_column <- function(column_name) {
    if (column_name %in% names(wfo_best)) as.character(wfo_best[[column_name]]) else character()
  }

  taxonomy_lookup <- tibble(
    input_name            = take_wfo_column("input_name"),
    matched               = as.logical(take_wfo_column("Matched")),
    fuzzy                 = as.logical(take_wfo_column("Fuzzy")),
    taxon_rank            = tolower(take_wfo_column("taxonRank")),
    accepted_species_name = take_wfo_column("scientificName"),
    taxonomic_status      = take_wfo_column("taxonomicStatus"),
    family                = take_wfo_column("family"),
    wfo_taxon_id          = take_wfo_column("taxonID")
  ) %>%
    mutate(across(c(accepted_species_name, taxonomic_status, family, wfo_taxon_id),
                  ~ if_else(matched %in% TRUE & is_filled(.x), .x, NA_character_)),
           species_level = matched %in% TRUE & taxon_rank %in% species_level_ranks,
           # Approximate matches can point to the wrong species, so only exact
           # matches are accepted.
           accepted = species_level & !fuzzy %in% TRUE)

  # Names matched only at genus or family keep their family but get no accepted
  # species name.
  lookup_index  <- match(name_for_matching, taxonomy_lookup$input_name)
  accepted_name <- taxonomy_lookup$accepted[lookup_index] %in% TRUE
  exact_match   <- taxonomy_lookup$matched[lookup_index] %in% TRUE & !taxonomy_lookup$fuzzy[lookup_index] %in% TRUE
  working_data$accepted_species_name <- if_else(accepted_name, taxonomy_lookup$accepted_species_name[lookup_index], NA_character_)
  working_data$taxonomic_status      <- if_else(accepted_name, taxonomy_lookup$taxonomic_status[lookup_index], NA_character_)
  working_data$family                <- if_else(exact_match, taxonomy_lookup$family[lookup_index], NA_character_)
  working_data$wfo_taxon_id          <- if_else(accepted_name, taxonomy_lookup$wfo_taxon_id[lookup_index], NA_character_)

  fuzzy_match <- taxonomy_lookup$fuzzy[lookup_index] %in% TRUE
  record_issues("species names", which(fuzzy_match), species_variable, recorded_species[fuzzy_match],
                "approximate (fuzzy) match to WFO not accepted", "warning",
                "no accepted name; confirm through the corrections list")

  not_submitted <- name_for_matching %in% unmatchable_names
  record_issues("species names", which(not_submitted), species_variable, recorded_species[not_submitted],
                "not a recognisable scientific name", "warning",
                "no accepted name; correct through the corrections list")

  species_review <- tibble(recorded_name = recorded_species, name_used = name_for_matching) %>%
    filter(!is.na(name_used)) %>%
    left_join(taxonomy_lookup, by = c("name_used" = "input_name")) %>%
    filter(!accepted %in% TRUE) %>%
    count(recorded_name, name_used, result = case_when(
      name_used %in% unmatchable_names ~ "not submitted: not a recognisable scientific name",
      !matched %in% TRUE ~ "no match",
      fuzzy %in% TRUE    ~ paste("approximate match, not accepted:", accepted_species_name),
      TRUE               ~ paste("matched at", taxon_rank, "level only")), name = "records") %>%
    arrange(desc(records))
}

# Baobab records are A. digitata by tree type.
is_baobab <- working_data[[tree_type_variable]] %in% "baobab"
working_data$accepted_species_name[is_baobab] <- "Adansonia digitata"

# Records of sensitive species are removed from the public file with their
# photographs (Step 10), because a position or a photograph would expose the
# tree. A record counts as sensitive if its recorded, corrected or accepted
# name is a listed species or one of its infraspecific taxa.
is_sensitive <- function(names) {
  names <- tolower(str_squish(coalesce(names, "")))
  Reduce(`|`, lapply(tolower(sensitive_species), function(species) names == species |
                       startsWith(names, paste0(species, " "))), FALSE)
}
sensitive_record <- is_sensitive(recorded_species) | is_sensitive(name_for_matching) |
  is_sensitive(working_data$accepted_species_name)
record_issues("species names", which(sensitive_record), species_variable, NA,
              "sensitive species", "error", "record and photographs removed from the public file")
```

`r if (wfo_backbone_available) paste0(format(sum(is_filled(working_data$accepted_species_name)), big.mark = ","), " of the ", format(sum(is_filled(recorded_species)), big.mark = ","), " records with a species name were matched to an accepted species in the WFO backbone. Names without a species-level match are listed in species_name_review.csv; adding them to the corrections list resolves them in the next run.") else paste0("The WFO backbone was not found at ", input_paths$wfo_backbone_file, ", so taxonomic matching was not carried out and the taxonomy columns are empty. Download classification.csv from World Flora Online and set its path in the document parameters.")`

```{r}
#| results: asis
show_step_results("species names", "Species name checks.")
if (nrow(species_review) > 0) {
  cat("\n")
  print(report_table(species_review, "Species names without a species-level match, or matched approximately.",
                     maximum_rows = 30))
}
```

# Step 10: Tree observations, sensitive species and duplicates

A record enters the public file only if it is positively identified as an observation of a tree: it must hold a value for at least one attribute of a tree (a stem, height or crown measurement, the number of stems, planting, phenology, condition, damage or a photograph) or a species name recorded by the observer. Records of GPS track and route points are removed whatever they hold. A stem measurement is not required, so a well-located tree recorded only with a photograph or a species name is kept, while track points, transect waypoints and plot coordinates are removed. The records removed at this stage are listed by source file in `tree_evidence_review.csv` and record by record in `records_without_tree_evidence.csv`, so that each source can be checked. Records of sensitive species are then removed.

Duplicates are screened only among the records that passed all earlier checks, so a copy kept is never one removed for another reason. A tree is identified by its source file, sheet, section and identifier, because files holding several plots often number the trees of each plot from 1. Five rules are applied in turn: (1) exact duplicates; (2) the same tree recorded twice on one date; (3) different trees at the same position in one file, such as a plot centre copied to every tree, where every record at that position is removed, because the position is not that of the tree (where the trees share one row of a paired form, they are flagged instead); (4) the same position, full date and tree type in different files; and (5) near-duplicates without an identifier: records from different files or sheets of the same tree type within `r near_duplicate_metres` m of each other, with stem circumferences within `r 100 * near_duplicate_circumference_tolerance`% and compatible dates, which catches versions of one survey with rounded positions. Under rules 2, 4 and 5 the most complete record is kept (the earlier if equally complete).

```{r}
#| label: tree-observation-and-duplicate-checks

dictionary_variables <- dictionary$variable_name
column_or_empty <- function(name) if (name %in% names(working_data)) working_data[[name]] else
  rep(NA_character_, number_of_records)

values_per_record <- rowSums(as.data.frame(lapply(working_data[dictionary_variables], is_filled)))
empty_record <- values_per_record == 0
record_issues("duplicates", which(empty_record), "(whole record)", NA, "record has no values",
              "error", "record removed")

# Evidence that a record is an observation of a tree, from the values recorded
# (taken before the elephant damage check of Step 8 emptied any).
evidence_present <- as.data.frame(lapply(tree_evidence_values, is_filled))
names(evidence_present) <- tree_evidence_variables
species_source <- column_or_empty("source_species")
species_recorded_by_observer <- is_filled(working_data[[species_variable]]) &
  species_source %in% species_sources_counting_as_evidence
has_tree_attribute   <- rowSums(evidence_present) > 0
listed_location_file <- coalesce(working_data$source_file %in% files_recording_tree_locations, FALSE)
gps_track_point      <- coalesce(tolower(column_or_empty("source_sheet")) %in% gps_track_layers, FALSE)
is_tree_observation  <- (has_tree_attribute | species_recorded_by_observer | listed_location_file) &
  !gps_track_point
has_stem_measurement <- rowSums(as.data.frame(lapply(working_data[stem_measurement_variables], is_filled))) > 0

# Removals before duplicate screening, counted once each in this order:
# coordinates, study region, measurements, tree observation, sensitive species.
missing_position <- is.na(latitude) | is.na(longitude)
removed_no_position <- !empty_record & require_coordinates_in_public_file & missing_position
removed_imprecise   <- !empty_record & !removed_no_position & remove_imprecise_positions & imprecise
removed_coordinates <- removed_no_position | removed_imprecise
removed_outside     <- !empty_record & !removed_coordinates & outside_study_region
removed_implausible <- !empty_record & !removed_coordinates & !removed_outside & implausible_measurement
reached_tree_check  <- !empty_record & !removed_coordinates & !removed_outside & !removed_implausible
removed_not_tree    <- reached_tree_check & !is_tree_observation
removed_gps_track   <- removed_not_tree & gps_track_point
removed_sensitive   <- reached_tree_check & !removed_not_tree & sensitive_record
removed_measurement <- removed_implausible  # kept for the data quality table

record_issues("public file", which(removed_no_position), pair_name, NA, "latitude or longitude missing",
              "error", "record removed")
record_issues("public file", which(removed_gps_track), "source_sheet", column_or_empty("source_sheet")[removed_gps_track],
              "GPS track or route point", "error", "record removed")
record_issues("public file", which(removed_not_tree & !removed_gps_track), "(whole record)", NA,
              "no attribute of a tree and no species recorded by the observer", "error", "record removed")
record_issues("public file", which(reached_tree_check & listed_location_file & !has_tree_attribute &
                                     !species_recorded_by_observer),
              "(whole record)", NA, "tree recorded for its location only (files_recording_tree_locations)",
              "note", "record kept")
record_issues("public file", which(removed_sensitive), species_variable, NA,
              paste("record of a sensitive species (", paste(sensitive_species, collapse = ", "), ")"),
              "error", "record and photographs removed")

# How each source fared at the tree-observation check, for review. The
# records compared are those that reached the check without a stem
# measurement, the records the earlier stem-measurement rule removed.
floral_trait_variables <- intersect(na.omit(variable_for("floral_traits")), names(evidence_present))
evidence_kind <- function(rows) {
  kinds <- cbind(
    photograph = rowSums(evidence_present[rows, intersect(photograph_variables, names(evidence_present)), drop = FALSE]) > 0,
    size = rowSums(evidence_present[rows, intersect(c(variable_for("height"), variable_for("crown_1"),
                                                      variable_for("crown_2")), names(evidence_present)), drop = FALSE]) > 0,
    `phenology, condition or stems` = rowSums(evidence_present[rows, setdiff(names(evidence_present),
      c(stem_measurement_variables, photograph_variables, floral_trait_variables, variable_for("height"),
        variable_for("crown_1"), variable_for("crown_2"))), drop = FALSE]) > 0,
    `floral traits` = rowSums(evidence_present[rows, floral_trait_variables, drop = FALSE]) > 0,
    `species named by the observer` = species_recorded_by_observer[rows])
  apply(kinds, 1, function(row) if (any(row)) paste(colnames(kinds)[row], collapse = " + ") else "")
}
without_stem <- reached_tree_check & !has_stem_measurement
review_rows  <- which(without_stem)
tree_evidence_review <- tibble(
  source_file  = working_data$source_file[review_rows],
  source_sheet = column_or_empty("source_sheet")[review_rows],
  result = case_when(removed_gps_track[review_rows] ~ "removed: GPS track or route point",
                     removed_not_tree[review_rows]  ~ "removed: no evidence of a tree",
                     listed_location_file[review_rows] & !has_tree_attribute[review_rows] &
                       !species_recorded_by_observer[review_rows] ~ "kept: file of tree locations",
                     TRUE ~ paste("kept:", evidence_kind(review_rows)))) %>%
  count(source_file, source_sheet, result, name = "records") %>%
  arrange(source_file, source_sheet, desc(records))

filled_matrix <- as.matrix(as.data.frame(lapply(working_data[dictionary_variables], is_filled)))
filled_variables <- apply(filled_matrix, 1, function(row) paste(dictionary_variables[row], collapse = ", "))
records_without_tree_evidence <- tibble(
  record_number = which(removed_not_tree),
  source_file   = working_data$source_file[removed_not_tree],
  source_sheet  = column_or_empty("source_sheet")[removed_not_tree],
  source_row    = column_or_empty("source_row")[removed_not_tree],
  reason        = if_else(removed_gps_track[removed_not_tree], "GPS track or route point", "no evidence of a tree"),
  tree_id       = if (!is.na(tree_identity_variable)) working_data[[tree_identity_variable]][removed_not_tree] else NA_character_,
  comments      = if (length(comment_variables) > 0) do.call(paste, c(lapply(working_data[comment_variables],
                    function(x) coalesce(x, "")), sep = " "))[removed_not_tree] else NA_character_,
  values_present = filled_variables[removed_not_tree])

# Duplicates are screened only among records that passed those checks, so the
# copy kept is never one removed for another reason.
passed_checks <- reached_tree_check & !removed_not_tree & !removed_sensitive
record_text <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(working_data[dictionary_variables],
                                       function(values) coalesce(values, "\u0001")),
                                sep = "\u0002"))
record_text[!passed_checks] <- NA
first_copy       <- match(record_text, record_text)
duplicate_record <- passed_checks & first_copy != seq_len(number_of_records)
record_issues("duplicates", which(duplicate_record), "(whole record)",
              paste("same as record", first_copy[duplicate_record]),
              "rule 1: exact duplicate of an earlier record", "error", "record removed")
kept_so_far <- passed_checks & !duplicate_record

# A tree is identified by its file, sheet, section and identifier.
tree_identifier <- if (!is.na(tree_identity_variable)) working_data[[tree_identity_variable]] else
  rep(NA_character_, number_of_records)
tree_key <- ifelse(is_filled(tree_identifier),
                   paste(working_data$source_file, coalesce(column_or_empty("source_sheet"), ""),
                         coalesce(column_or_empty("source_section"), ""),
                         str_to_lower(str_squish(tree_identifier)), sep = " | "),
                   NA_character_)

candidates <- tibble(
  record_number = seq_len(number_of_records), values = values_per_record,
  source_file = working_data$source_file, source_sheet = coalesce(column_or_empty("source_sheet"), ""),
  source_row = coalesce(column_or_empty("source_row"), ""),
  tree = tree_key, date = working_data[[date_variable]], day = str_sub(working_data[[date_variable]], 1, 10),
  position = paste(working_data[[latitude_variable]], working_data[[longitude_variable]]),
  lat = latitude, lon = longitude,
  type = coalesce(working_data[[tree_type_variable]], ""),
  circumference = as_number(working_data[[circumference_variable]]))

# same_occasion() is TRUE where two dates may be one visit: either date is
# missing, or one is the other written to a coarser precision.
same_occasion <- function(a, b) !is_filled(a) | !is_filled(b) | startsWith(coalesce(a, ""), coalesce(b, "")) |
  startsWith(coalesce(b, ""), coalesce(a, ""))
# similar_size() is TRUE where two circumferences differ by no more than the
# tolerance, as a proportion of the larger.
similar_size <- function(a, b) is.finite(a) & is.finite(b) &
  abs(a - b) <= near_duplicate_circumference_tolerance * pmax(a, b)
repeated_record <- rep(FALSE, number_of_records)

# Rule 2: the same tree recorded more than once on one date.
repeated_visit <- candidates %>%
  filter(kept_so_far, !is.na(tree), is_filled(date)) %>%
  group_by(tree, date) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>%
  arrange(desc(values), record_number, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(kept_record = first(record_number)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(record_number != kept_record)
record_issues("duplicates", repeated_visit$record_number, tree_identity_variable, repeated_visit$tree,
              paste("rule 2: same tree recorded again on the same date; record", repeated_visit$kept_record, "kept"),
              "error", "record removed")
repeated_record <- repeated_record | seq_len(number_of_records) %in% repeated_visit$record_number
kept_so_far <- kept_so_far & !repeated_record

# Rule 3: different trees at one position in one file, such as a copied plot
# centre. Two records are different trees if their identifiers differ, or, on
# one occasion, if their tree types or stem circumferences differ. Every
# record at such a position is removed, because the position is not that of
# the tree; the trees of one row of a paired form are flagged instead.
position_groups <- candidates %>%
  filter(kept_so_far, !is.na(lat)) %>%
  group_by(source_file, position) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>%
  ungroup()
copied_position_records <- integer()
shared_row_position_records <- integer()
for (group in split(position_groups, list(position_groups$source_file, position_groups$position), drop = TRUE)) {
  pair <- combn(nrow(group), 2)
  a <- pair[1, ]; b <- pair[2, ]
  both_identified <- !is.na(group$tree[a]) & !is.na(group$tree[b])
  different_trees <- (both_identified & group$tree[a] != group$tree[b]) |
    (!both_identified & same_occasion(group$day[a], group$day[b]) &
       (group$type[a] != group$type[b] |
          (is.finite(group$circumference[a]) & is.finite(group$circumference[b]) &
             !similar_size(group$circumference[a], group$circumference[b]))))
  if (!any(different_trees)) next
  one_form_row <- n_distinct(paste(group$source_sheet, group$source_row)) == 1
  if (one_form_row) {
    shared_row_position_records <- c(shared_row_position_records, group$record_number)
  } else {
    copied_position_records <- c(copied_position_records, group$record_number)
  }
}
record_issues("duplicates", copied_position_records, pair_name, candidates$position[copied_position_records],
              "rule 3: position shared by different trees in one file (copied position)", "error", "record removed")
record_issues("duplicates", shared_row_position_records, pair_name, candidates$position[shared_row_position_records],
              "rule 3: position shared by the trees of one form row", "warning", "kept; please confirm")
repeated_record <- repeated_record | seq_len(number_of_records) %in% copied_position_records
kept_so_far <- kept_so_far & !repeated_record

# Rule 4: the same observation in two or more files: same position (to 5
# decimal places, about 1 m), same full date and same tree type. Records on
# different dates are kept as repeat visits.
cross_file_repeat <- candidates %>%
  filter(kept_so_far, !is.na(lat), str_detect(coalesce(day, ""), "^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$")) %>%
  group_by(position, day, type) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(source_file) > 1) %>%
  arrange(desc(values), record_number, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(kept_file = first(source_file), kept_record = first(record_number)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(source_file != kept_file)
record_issues("duplicates", cross_file_repeat$record_number, pair_name,
              paste(cross_file_repeat$position, cross_file_repeat$day),
              paste("rule 4: same position and date as record", cross_file_repeat$kept_record,
                    "in", cross_file_repeat$kept_file, "(kept)"), "error", "record removed")
repeated_record <- repeated_record | seq_len(number_of_records) %in% cross_file_repeat$record_number
kept_so_far <- kept_so_far & !repeated_record

# Rule 5: near-duplicates without an identifier. Records from different files
# or sheets, of the same tree type, within near_duplicate_metres of each
# other, with similar circumferences and compatible dates are grouped; the
# most complete record of each group is kept, and the others are removed
# unless they come from the same file and sheet as the record kept.
near_duplicate_records <- integer()
near_pool <- filter(candidates, kept_so_far, !is.na(lat), is.finite(circumference))
if (nrow(near_pool) > 1) {
  sf_use_s2(TRUE)
  pool_points <- st_as_sf(near_pool, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)
  neighbours  <- st_is_within_distance(pool_points, dist = near_duplicate_metres)
  pairs <- tibble(a = rep(seq_along(neighbours), lengths(neighbours)), b = unlist(neighbours)) %>%
    filter(a < b)
  source_key <- paste(near_pool$source_file, near_pool$source_sheet)
  pairs <- pairs %>%
    filter(source_key[a] != source_key[b], near_pool$type[a] == near_pool$type[b],
           similar_size(near_pool$circumference[a], near_pool$circumference[b]),
           same_occasion(near_pool$day[a], near_pool$day[b]))
  if (nrow(pairs) > 0) {
    # Records linked by any chain of pairs form one group.
    group_of <- seq_len(nrow(near_pool))
    repeat {
      before <- group_of
      lowest <- pmin(group_of[pairs$a], group_of[pairs$b])
      lowest_by_record <- tapply(c(lowest, lowest), c(pairs$a, pairs$b), min)
      linked <- as.integer(names(lowest_by_record))
      group_of[linked] <- pmin(group_of[linked], lowest_by_record)
      group_of <- group_of[group_of]
      if (identical(before, group_of)) break
    }
    near_groups <- near_pool %>%
      mutate(group = group_of, key = source_key) %>%
      group_by(group) %>%
      filter(n() > 1) %>%
      arrange(desc(values), record_number, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
      mutate(kept_record = first(record_number), kept_key = first(key)) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      filter(record_number != kept_record, key != kept_key)
    near_duplicate_records <- near_groups$record_number
    record_issues("duplicates", near_groups$record_number, pair_name, near_groups$position,
                  paste0("rule 5: near-duplicate of record ", near_groups$kept_record, " (within ",
                         near_duplicate_metres, " m, same tree type, similar circumference)"),
                  "error", "record removed")
  }
}
repeated_record <- repeated_record | seq_len(number_of_records) %in% near_duplicate_records
```

# Step 11: Observation comments

Typing errors in the observers' comments are corrected with the list in `comment_corrections.csv` (input tables folder), which gives each error as recorded and its correction (for example, "Wholes" to "Holes" and "Gauging" to "Gouging"). A correction is applied only where the listed text stands as a whole word, in any letter case, and a capital first letter is kept. Every comment changed is logged with its original and corrected text in `qaqc_corrections_applied.csv`. `r if (check_comment_spelling) paste0("The corrected comments are then checked with the hunspell spelling checker (", spelling_dictionary, " dictionary). Words it does not recognise are listed with suggested corrections in comment_spelling_review.csv; they are not changed. A word confirmed as an error is corrected by adding it to comment_corrections.csv. The checker cannot find a real word used in error, such as \"wholes\" for \"holes\", so these are found by reading the comments.") else ""`

```{r}
#| label: comment-corrections

comment_corrections <- read_correction_table(input_paths$comment_corrections_file,
                                             "text_as_recorded", "corrected_text")
if (!file.exists(input_paths$comment_corrections_file)) {
  print_to_console("comment_corrections.csv was not found in ", input_tables_folder,
                   "; comments are not corrected.")
}

# Each listed correction is applied to every comment variable in turn, and the
# number of comments it changed is counted.
comment_correction_counts <- comment_corrections %>%
  select(text_as_recorded, corrected_text) %>%
  mutate(comments_corrected = 0L)
for (variable in comment_variables) {
  comments_before <- working_data[[variable]]
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(comment_corrections))) {
    values  <- working_data[[variable]]
    updated <- correct_comment_text(values, comment_corrections$text_as_recorded[i],
                                    comment_corrections$corrected_text[i])
    comment_correction_counts$comments_corrected[i] <- comment_correction_counts$comments_corrected[i] +
      sum(coalesce(updated != values, FALSE))
    working_data[[variable]] <- updated
  }
  comment_changed <- coalesce(comments_before != working_data[[variable]], FALSE)
  record_issues("comments", which(comment_changed), variable, comments_before[comment_changed],
                "typing error listed in comment_corrections.csv", "note", "text corrected")
  record_corrections("comments", which(comment_changed), variable, comments_before[comment_changed],
                     working_data[[variable]][comment_changed], "comment_corrections.csv")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: comment-spelling

# Words not recognised by hunspell are listed for review. Words in the
# accepted list, species names, country names and words containing digits or
# written in capitals (abbreviations) are not listed.
comment_spelling_review <- tibble(word = character(), occurrences = integer(), records = integer(),
                                  suggestions = character(), example_comment = character())
spelling_checked <- FALSE
if (check_comment_spelling && length(comment_variables) > 0) {
  if (!requireNamespace("hunspell", quietly = TRUE)) {
    print_to_console("The hunspell package is not installed; the spelling check of comments is skipped. ",
                     "Install it with install.packages(\"hunspell\").")
  } else {
    spelling_checked <- TRUE
    comment_text <- tibble(record_number = rep(seq_len(number_of_records), length(comment_variables)),
                           comment = unlist(working_data[comment_variables], use.names = FALSE)) %>%
      filter(is_filled(comment))
    known_words <- unique(c(words_accepted_in_comments,
                            unlist(str_split(na.omit(working_data[[species_variable]]), "\\s+")),
                            unlist(str_split(na.omit(working_data$country), "\\s+"))))
    unrecognised <- hunspell::hunspell(comment_text$comment, ignore = known_words,
                                       dict = hunspell::dictionary(spelling_dictionary))
    flagged_words <- tibble(record_number = rep(comment_text$record_number, lengths(unrecognised)),
                            comment = rep(comment_text$comment, lengths(unrecognised)),
                            word = as.character(unlist(unrecognised))) %>%
      filter(!str_detect(word, "\\d"), word != str_to_upper(word), nchar(word) > 2)
    if (nrow(flagged_words) > 0) {
      comment_spelling_review <- flagged_words %>%
        group_by(word) %>%
        summarise(occurrences = n(), records = n_distinct(record_number),
                  example_comment = str_trunc(first(comment), 100), .groups = "drop") %>%
        arrange(desc(occurrences), word)
      comment_spelling_review$suggestions <- vapply(
        hunspell::hunspell_suggest(comment_spelling_review$word, dict = hunspell::dictionary(spelling_dictionary)),
        function(found) paste(head(found, 3), collapse = ", "), character(1))
      comment_spelling_review <- relocate(comment_spelling_review, suggestions, .after = records)
      record_issues("comments", unique(flagged_words$record_number), paste(comment_variables, collapse = ", "),
                    NA, "word not recognised by the spelling checker", "note", "kept; listed for review")
    }
    print_to_console("\nSpelling check of comments: ", nrow(comment_spelling_review),
                     " words not recognised; see comment_spelling_review.csv")
  }
}
```

# Public data file

The public file, `r input_paths$public_file_name`, is saved in its own folder (`public_data`). It contains the record identifier, the dictionary variables in dictionary order, except those withheld (`r paste(dictionary$variable_name[dictionary$withheld & dictionary$kind != "email"], collapse = ", ")` and the email address), followed by the published derived variables in @tbl-derived`r if (publish_source_columns) " and the source columns" else ""`. `r if (!publish_source_columns) "The source columns, which record the file, sheet and row of each record, are not published; they remain in the internal reports." else ""` The tree identifier is withheld, because contributors reuse identifiers such as "1" or "T1" across files; it remains in the internal files, where the duplicate checks use it. DBH is withheld, because a circumference is calculated from it where none was measured (Step 6); calculated circumferences are not marked in the public file. Email addresses are removed: the email variable is withheld, and any email address written inside another value (for example, a comment) is replaced by "\[email address removed\]". Observer names are published only as names from the contributor list (Step 2) and only where the observer answered "yes" to the visibility question; where the answer is "no", "unknown" or blank, observer_name shows "`r anonymous_label`" (Step 3). Only records `r if (include_african_islands) "in Africa" else "on mainland Africa"` are included (Step 5). A record is removed if its latitude or longitude is missing, if it is not positively identified as a tree observation, or if it is a record of a sensitive species, whose photographs are not copied either (Step 10). Duplicates are removed by the five rules of Step 10, among the records that passed every other check. Each record carries its data collection method (`data_collection_method`), the name of the raw-input folder that holds its source file. Observation dates are written as ISO 8601 dates without a time: `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `YYYY-MM` and `YYYY` where the day or month was not recorded. Every empty value is written as NA.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-derived
#| tbl-cap: "Variables derived during quality control. Only those marked yes are written to the public file."
knitr::kable(rename(derived_variables, Variable = variable_name, Published = in_public,
                    Description = description),
             format = "pipe")
```

```{r}
#| label: build-public-file

# Records kept: those that passed every check and were not removed as
# duplicates (Step 10).
keep_record <- passed_checks & !duplicate_record & !repeated_record

if (!is.na(observer_name_variable)) working_data[[observer_name_variable]][names_withheld] <- anonymous_label

# Identifiers come from the source file, sheet, row and column group, so they
# persist across releases.
identity_columns <- intersect(c("source_file", "source_sheet", "source_row", "source_column_group"), names(working_data))
source_key <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(working_data[identity_columns], coalesce, ""), sep = "|"))
source_hash <- unname(vapply(source_key, digest::digest, character(1), algo = "md5", serialize = FALSE))
working_data$record_id <- paste0(record_id_prefix, "-", toupper(substr(source_hash, 1, 10)))
if (anyDuplicated(working_data$record_id[keep_record]) > 0) {
  stop("Two records received the same record identifier.", call. = FALSE)
}

# Photographs are copied under names derived from the record identifier;
# sub-folders are searched too.

# photo_name_key() reduces a photograph reference or path to a lower-case file
# name without extension.
photo_name_key <- function(references) {
  cleaned <- vapply(coalesce(references, ""), function(text) {
    tryCatch(utils::URLdecode(text), error = function(e) text)
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  cleaned <- str_replace_all(cleaned, "\\\\", "/")
  file_names <- str_extract_all(cleaned, "[^/?=&#]+\\.[A-Za-z0-9]{2,5}(?=$|[?&#])")
  last_name  <- vapply(file_names, function(found) if (length(found)) found[length(found)] else NA_character_,
                       character(1))
  last_name  <- coalesce(last_name, basename(cleaned))
  tolower(tools::file_path_sans_ext(last_name))
}

photo_lookup <- tibble()
if (is_filled(input_paths$photo_source_folder)) {
  photo_folder_out <- file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "photographs_for_public")
  # The folder is emptied first, so that no photograph copied by an earlier
  # run (for example, of a record since removed) remains in it.
  unlink(photo_folder_out, recursive = TRUE)
  dir.create(photo_folder_out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  photo_files <- list.files(input_paths$photo_source_folder,
                            pattern = "\\.(jpe?g|png|gif|bmp|tiff?|heic|webp)$",
                            ignore.case = TRUE, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  message("Photographs found in ", input_paths$photo_source_folder, " and its sub-folders: ",
          length(photo_files))
  photo_key <- photo_name_key(photo_files)

  # File names found in several sub-folders cannot be matched safely and are
  # not copied.
  repeated_keys <- unique(photo_key[duplicated(photo_key)])

  for (photo_number in seq_along(photograph_variables)) {
    variable  <- photograph_variables[photo_number]
    reference <- working_data[[variable]]
    reference_key <- photo_name_key(reference)
    file_index <- match(reference_key, photo_key)

    ambiguous <- keep_record & is_filled(reference) & reference_key %in% repeated_keys
    record_issues("photographs", which(ambiguous), variable, reference[ambiguous],
                  "photograph file name found in more than one sub-folder", "warning",
                  "photograph not copied; rename the files so that each name is unique")

    not_found <- keep_record & is_filled(reference) & is.na(file_index)
    record_issues("photographs", which(not_found), variable, reference[not_found],
                  "photograph file not found in the photo folder", "warning", "reference kept")

    found <- keep_record & !is.na(file_index) & !ambiguous
    new_names <- paste0(working_data$record_id[found], "_", photo_number, ".",
                        tolower(tools::file_ext(photo_files[file_index[found]])))
    file.copy(photo_files[file_index[found]], file.path(photo_folder_out, new_names), overwrite = TRUE)
    photo_lookup <- bind_rows(photo_lookup, tibble(record_id = working_data$record_id[found],
                                                   variable_name = variable,
                                                   original_reference = reference[found],
                                                   public_file_name = new_names))
    working_data[[variable]][found] <- new_names
  }
}

record_flags <- current_issues() %>%
  filter(!is.na(record_number), severity %in% c("error", "warning"),
         !action_taken %in% c("record removed")) %>%
  distinct(record_number, flag = paste0(check, " (", variable_name, ")")) %>%
  group_by(record_number) %>%
  summarise(qaqc_flags = paste(flag, collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop")
working_data$qaqc_flags <- record_flags$qaqc_flags[match(seq_len(number_of_records),
                                                         record_flags$record_number)]

# All kept records with every column, for the internal reports only.
kept_records <- working_data[keep_record, ]

public_variables <- dictionary$variable_name[!dictionary$withheld]
public_columns <- c("record_id", public_variables, setdiff(published_derived_variables, "record_id"),
                    if (publish_source_columns) source_columns)
public_dataset <- working_data[keep_record, public_columns]
public_record_numbers <- which(keep_record)

# Observation dates are published without a time; partial dates keep only the
# parts recorded (YYYY-MM or YYYY).
public_dataset[[date_variable]] <- str_sub(public_dataset[[date_variable]], 1, 10)

columns_not_published <- c(dictionary$variable_name[dictionary$withheld],
                           setdiff(derived_variables$variable_name, published_derived_variables),
                           if (!publish_source_columns) source_columns)

# E-mail addresses written inside any value are removed.
for (column in public_columns) {
  values <- public_dataset[[column]]
  contains_email <- is_filled(values) & str_detect(values, email_address_pattern)
  record_issues("public file", public_record_numbers[contains_email], column, NA,
                "email address found in text", "note", "email address replaced")
  public_dataset[[column]][contains_email] <-
    str_replace_all(values[contains_email], email_address_pattern, "[email address removed]")
}
for (variable in dictionary$variable_name[dictionary$withheld]) {
  record_issues("public file", NA, variable, NA, "personal data", "note", "variable withheld")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: final-verification

# Final checks
# No withheld column is present.
confirm(!any(columns_not_published %in% names(public_dataset)),
        paste("a withheld column is still present:",
              paste(intersect(columns_not_published, names(public_dataset)), collapse = ", ")))
confirm(!any(str_starts(names(public_dataset), fixed(source_column_prefix))) || publish_source_columns,
        "a source column is still present.")
# No e-mail address appears anywhere.
confirm(!any(map_lgl(public_dataset, ~ any(str_detect(.x, email_address_pattern), na.rm = TRUE))),
        "an email address is still present.")
# The tree identifier and DBH are withheld.
confirm(!any(c(tree_identity_variable, dbh_variable, dbh_two_variable) %in% names(public_dataset)),
        "the tree identifier or DBH is still in the public file.")
confirm(all(follows_dictionary_style(names(public_dataset))),
        "a column name does not follow the dictionary format.")
confirm(identical(intersect(names(public_dataset), dictionary$variable_name), public_variables),
        "the dictionary variables are not in dictionary order.")
coordinate_format <- paste0("^-?\\d{1,3}\\.\\d{", coordinate_decimal_places, "}$")
confirm(all(str_detect(na.omit(c(public_dataset[[latitude_variable]], public_dataset[[longitude_variable]])),
                       coordinate_format)),
        "a coordinate does not have the required number of decimal places.")
confirm(all(is.na(public_dataset[[latitude_variable]]) == is.na(public_dataset[[longitude_variable]])),
        "a record has only one coordinate.")
if (require_coordinates_in_public_file) {
  confirm(!any(is.na(public_dataset[[latitude_variable]]) | is.na(public_dataset[[longitude_variable]])),
          "a record has a missing latitude or longitude.")
}
# No record logged as removed by any check (including every duplicate rule)
# is in the public file.
removed_by_a_check <- current_issues() %>%
  filter(action_taken %in% c("record removed", "record and photographs removed")) %>%
  pull(record_number)
confirm(!any(public_record_numbers %in% removed_by_a_check),
        "a record logged as removed (for example, a duplicate) is in the public file.")
# Every public record is a tree observation, and none is of a sensitive
# species.
confirm(all(is_tree_observation[public_record_numbers]), "a public record is not a tree observation.")
confirm(!any(sensitive_record[public_record_numbers]), "a record of a sensitive species is in the public file.")
# Every kept circumference has a source in the internal records, and the
# source is not published.
confirm(all(is_filled(kept_records$circumference_source) ==
              (is_filled(kept_records[[circumference_variable]]) |
                 (if (!is.na(stem_two_variable)) is_filled(kept_records[[stem_two_variable]]) else FALSE))),
        "a stem circumference has no circumference_source, or a source has no circumference.")
confirm(!"circumference_source" %in% names(public_dataset), "circumference_source is in the public file.")
confirm(!any(c("floral_traits", variable_for("floral_traits")) %in% names(public_dataset)),
        "the floral trait measurements are in the public file.")
# No photograph of a removed record is in the folder of public photographs.
if (exists("photo_folder_out")) {
  confirm(all(sub("_\\d+\\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$", "", list.files(photo_folder_out)) %in% public_dataset$record_id),
          "the folder of public photographs holds a photograph of a record not in the public file.")
}
confirm(!any(outside_study_region[public_record_numbers]),
        "a record lies outside the study region.")
confirm(all(is_filled(public_dataset$record_id)) && anyDuplicated(public_dataset$record_id) == 0,
        "record identifiers are missing or repeated.")
confirm(all(str_detect(na.omit(public_dataset[[date_variable]]), "^\\d{4}(-\\d{2}(-\\d{2})?)?$")),
        "an observation date is not an ISO 8601 date without a time.")
confirm(!species_variable %in% names(public_dataset) || !"species" %in% withheld_from_public_file,
        "the species as recorded is still in the public file.")
# Rounded values have no more decimal places than set.
for (role_name in names(decimal_places_by_role)) {
  variable <- variable_for(role_name)
  if (is.na(variable) || !variable %in% names(public_dataset)) next
  confirm(all(count_decimal_places(na.omit(public_dataset[[variable]])) <= decimal_places_by_role[[role_name]]),
          paste(variable, "has more decimal places than set in decimal_places_by_role."))
}
# Every observer who did not answer "yes" is shown as "Anonymous".
if (!is.na(observer_name_variable) && withhold_names_answered_no) {
  not_yes <- visibility_answers[public_record_numbers] != "yes"
  confirm(all(public_dataset[[observer_name_variable]][not_yes & is_filled(public_dataset[[observer_name_variable]])] %in%
                anonymous_label),
          "a name is published although the observer did not answer yes.")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: save-outputs

# The full issue log is for internal use only, as it holds original values.
record_identifiers <- tibble(record_number = seq_len(number_of_records),
                             record_id = working_data$record_id) %>%
  bind_cols(harmonised_data[intersect(c(tree_identity_variable, source_columns), names(harmonised_data))])
qaqc_issues <- current_issues() %>%
  left_join(record_identifiers, by = "record_number") %>%
  relocate(step, record_number, record_id) %>%
  arrange(factor(severity, levels = c("error", "warning", "note")), step, record_number)

# Each variable is described from, in order: the dictionary's
# variable_description column, the standard description of its role, the
# dictionary label, or the description of a derived variable.
dictionary_row <- match(names(public_dataset), dictionary$variable_name)
role_description <- standard_descriptions$description[match(dictionary$role[dictionary_row],
                                                            standard_descriptions$role)]
variable_summary <- tibble(variable_name = names(public_dataset)) %>%
  mutate(
    variable_description = coalesce(
      if_else(is_filled(dictionary$variable_description[dictionary_row]),
              dictionary$variable_description[dictionary_row], NA_character_),
      role_description,
      if_else(is_filled(dictionary$variable_label[dictionary_row]),
              dictionary$variable_label[dictionary_row], NA_character_),
      derived_variables$description[match(variable_name, derived_variables$variable_name)],
      if_else(str_starts(variable_name, fixed(source_column_prefix)),
              "Provenance of the record in the contributor's file.", NA_character_)),
    unit = coalesce(
      if_else(dictionary$kind[dictionary_row] %in% c("number", "whole_number") &
                is_filled(dictionary$unit_or_values[dictionary_row]),
              dictionary$unit_or_values[dictionary_row], NA_character_),
      standard_descriptions$unit[match(dictionary$role[dictionary_row], standard_descriptions$role)]),
    source = case_when(variable_name %in% dictionary$variable_name ~ "dictionary",
                       variable_name %in% derived_variables$variable_name ~ "derived",
                       TRUE ~ "source column"),
    values_in_public_file = map_int(variable_name, ~ sum(is_filled(public_dataset[[.x]]))),
    percent_complete = round(100 * values_in_public_file / max(nrow(public_dataset), 1), 1)
  )
undescribed <- variable_summary$variable_name[is.na(variable_summary$variable_description)]
if (length(undescribed) > 0) {
  warning("No description was found for: ", paste(undescribed, collapse = ", "),
          ". Add a variable_description column to the dictionary.", call. = FALSE)
}

# The variable summary is also saved as a Word table in the Scientific Data
# style.
# The table of the manuscript (Data Records) defines every variable; its
# only figure is the completeness of each, which replaces a separate figure.
variable_table_text <- variable_summary %>%
  transmute(Variable = variable_name,
            Description = coalesce(variable_description, "\u2014"),
            Unit = coalesce(unit, "\u2014"),
            `Complete (%)` = formatC(percent_complete, format = "f", digits = 1))
variable_table_footnote <- paste0(
  "Variables in ", input_paths$public_file_name, ", in the order in which they appear. ",
  "Complete (%): percentage of records with a value. Units are given for numeric variables; ",
  "\u2014, not applicable. Coordinates use the WGS 84 datum. Empty values are written as NA.")
save_word_table(variable_table_text, variable_table_number, paste0("Variables in ", input_paths$public_file_name, "."),
                variable_table_footnote, column_widths = c(1.8, 3.1, 0.75, 0.75),
                right_aligned_columns = 4,
                path = file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "table_variable_summary.docx"))

# Records removed by each rule, each counted once at the first rule it
# fails (rules applied in the order listed), and records flagged by rule 3.
removals_by_rule <- tibble(
  stage = c("Initial data compilation", rep("Coordinate completeness and precision", 2),
            "Geographic boundary checks", "Measurement plausibility", rep("Tree observation present", 2),
            "Sensitive species", rep("Duplicate screening", 5), "Duplicate screening (flagged, kept)"),
  rule = c("record has no values", "latitude or longitude missing", "position recorded imprecisely",
           "outside mainland Africa", "stem, height or crown value beyond an error limit",
           "GPS track or route point", "no attribute of a tree and no species recorded by the observer",
           paste("record of", paste(sensitive_species, collapse = ", ")),
           "rule 1: exact duplicate", "rule 2: same tree on one date", "rule 3: copied position (all records at it)",
           "rule 4: same position, date and tree type in two files", "rule 5: near-duplicate",
           "rule 3: position shared by the trees of one form row"),
  records = c(sum(empty_record), sum(removed_no_position), sum(removed_imprecise), sum(removed_outside),
              sum(removed_implausible), sum(removed_gps_track), sum(removed_not_tree & !removed_gps_track),
              sum(removed_sensitive), sum(duplicate_record), nrow(repeated_visit),
              length(copied_position_records), nrow(cross_file_repeat), length(near_duplicate_records),
              length(shared_row_position_records)))

# Every value changed by a correction rule, linked to its record_id.
corrections_applied <- bind_rows(tibble(step = character(), record_number = integer(),
                                        variable_name = character(), original_value = character(),
                                        corrected_value = character(), rule = character()),
                                 correction_log) %>%
  left_join(record_identifiers, by = "record_number") %>%
  mutate(in_public_file = if_else(record_number %in% public_record_numbers, "yes", "no")) %>%
  relocate(step, record_number, record_id)

# Manuscript figures are computed from the public file so that text and data
# agree.
type_counts <- table(factor(public_dataset[[tree_type_variable]], levels = c("baobab", "non-baobab")), useNA = "always")
public_dates <- na.omit(str_sub(public_dataset[[date_variable]], 1, 10))
public_dates <- public_dates[str_detect(public_dates, "^\\d{4}")]
manuscript_numbers <- tibble(
  quantity = c("Records in the public file", "Baobab records", "Non-baobab records", "Records of unrecorded type",
               "Unique baobab locations", "Countries", "Country list", "Source files",
               "Earliest observation date", "Latest observation date", "Records without a date",
               "Records naming their observer", "Different observers named", "Records with an anonymous observer",
               "Records removed: no valid position", "Records removed: imprecise position",
               "Records removed: outside mainland Africa", "Records removed: exact duplicates",
               "Records removed: repeated records",
               "Records removed: not a tree observation", "Records removed: GPS track or route points",
               "Records removed: implausible measurement", "Records removed: sensitive species",
               "Sensitive species whose records were removed",
               "Records without a stem measurement that reached the tree-observation check",
               "Of these, kept as tree observations", "Public records without a stem circumference",
               "Records with a circumference calculated from DBH", "Records with a photograph",
               "Non-baobab records with an accepted species name", "Non-baobab records without an accepted species name",
               "Elephant damage values left empty (outside the elephant range)", "IUCN Red List version"),
  value = c(nrow(public_dataset), type_counts[["baobab"]], type_counts[["non-baobab"]], sum(is.na(public_dataset[[tree_type_variable]])),
            nrow(distinct(filter(public_dataset, .data[[tree_type_variable]] %in% "baobab"), .data[[latitude_variable]], .data[[longitude_variable]])),
            n_distinct(na.omit(public_dataset$country)), paste(sort(unique(na.omit(public_dataset$country))), collapse = ", "),
            n_distinct(kept_records$source_file),  # Source columns are not in the public file.
            if (length(public_dates)) min(public_dates) else NA, if (length(public_dates)) max(public_dates) else NA,
            sum(!is_filled(public_dataset[[date_variable]])),
            if (!is.na(observer_name_variable)) sum(is_filled(public_dataset[[observer_name_variable]]) &
                                                    !public_dataset[[observer_name_variable]] %in% anonymous_label) else NA,
            if (!is.na(observer_name_variable)) n_distinct(setdiff(unlist(str_split(na.omit(public_dataset[[observer_name_variable]]), "; ")),
                                                                   anonymous_label)) else NA,
            if (!is.na(observer_name_variable)) sum(public_dataset[[observer_name_variable]] %in% anonymous_label) else NA,
            sum(removed_no_position), sum(removed_imprecise),
            sum(removed_outside), sum(duplicate_record),
            sum(repeated_record), sum(removed_not_tree), sum(removed_gps_track), sum(removed_implausible),
            sum(removed_sensitive), paste(sensitive_species, collapse = ", "),
            sum(without_stem), sum(without_stem & !removed_not_tree),
            sum(!is_filled(public_dataset[[circumference_variable]])),
            sum(str_detect(coalesce(kept_records$circumference_source, ""), "calculated")),
            if (length(photograph_variables) > 0) sum(is_filled(public_dataset[[photograph_variables[1]]])) else NA,
            sum(public_dataset[[tree_type_variable]] %in% "non-baobab" & is_filled(public_dataset$accepted_species_name)),
            sum(public_dataset[[tree_type_variable]] %in% "non-baobab" & !is_filled(public_dataset$accepted_species_name)),
            sum(elephant_damage_outside_range[public_record_numbers]),
            if (is_filled(iucn_red_list_version)) iucn_red_list_version else "not recorded")
)
manuscript_numbers$value <- as.character(manuscript_numbers$value)

# Trees in the public file by data collection method and tree type.
collection_method_counts <- public_dataset %>%
  mutate(tree_type = coalesce(.data[[tree_type_variable]], "not recorded")) %>%
  count(data_collection_method, tree_type) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tree_type, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
for (type in c("baobab", "non-baobab")) {
  if (!type %in% names(collection_method_counts)) collection_method_counts[[type]] <- 0L
}
collection_method_counts <- collection_method_counts %>%
  relocate(data_collection_method, baobab, `non-baobab`) %>%
  mutate(total = rowSums(across(-data_collection_method))) %>%
  arrange(desc(total))
manuscript_numbers <- bind_rows(manuscript_numbers, tibble(
  quantity = c(paste("Records from data collection method:", collection_method_counts$data_collection_method),
               paste("Baobab records from data collection method:", collection_method_counts$data_collection_method),
               paste("Non-baobab records from data collection method:", collection_method_counts$data_collection_method)),
  value = as.character(c(collection_method_counts$total, collection_method_counts$baobab,
                         collection_method_counts$`non-baobab`))))

records_by_file <- kept_records %>%
  count(source_file, tree_type = coalesce(.data[[tree_type_variable]], "not recorded")) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tree_type, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  left_join(kept_records %>% group_by(source_file) %>%
              summarise(records = n(), countries = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(country))), collapse = ", "),
                        first_date = suppressWarnings(min(str_sub(.data[[date_variable]], 1, 10), na.rm = TRUE)),
                        last_date = suppressWarnings(max(str_sub(.data[[date_variable]], 1, 10), na.rm = TRUE)),
                        .groups = "drop"), by = "source_file") %>%
  arrange(desc(records))

# Flags, taxonomy and provenance are saved for internal review, linked by
# record_id.
record_flags_internal <- kept_records %>%
  select(record_id, any_of(c(tree_identity_variable, "circumference_source", "qaqc_flags",
                             "accepted_species_name", "taxonomic_status", "family", "wfo_taxon_id")),
         all_of(source_columns))

# write_excel_csv() keeps accented letters correct in Excel.
write_excel_csv(public_dataset, public_file_path, na = "NA")
write_excel_csv(qaqc_issues, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "qaqc_issues.csv"), na = "")
write_excel_csv(record_flags_internal, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "qaqc_record_flags.csv"), na = "")
write_excel_csv(manuscript_numbers, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "manuscript_numbers.csv"), na = "")
write_excel_csv(records_by_file, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "manuscript_table_records_by_file.csv"), na = "")
write_excel_csv(variable_summary, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "qaqc_variable_summary.csv"), na = "")
write_excel_csv(corrections_applied, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "qaqc_corrections_applied.csv"), na = "")
write_excel_csv(removals_by_rule, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "qaqc_removals_by_rule.csv"), na = "")
write_excel_csv(tree_evidence_review, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "tree_evidence_review.csv"), na = "")
write_excel_csv(records_without_tree_evidence, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "records_without_tree_evidence.csv"),
                na = "")
if (spelling_checked) {
  write_excel_csv(comment_spelling_review, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "comment_spelling_review.csv"),
                  na = "")
}
if (!is.na(observer_name_variable)) {
  write_excel_csv(observer_name_review, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "observer_name_review.csv"), na = "")
}
if (nrow(species_review) > 0) {
  write_excel_csv(species_review, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "species_name_review.csv"), na = "")
}
if (nrow(photo_lookup) > 0) {
  write_excel_csv(photo_lookup, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "photograph_name_lookup.csv"), na = "")
}
```

# Summary

```{r}
#| label: data-quality-numbers

# Records entering and leaving each validation stage. Each removed record is
# counted once, at the first stage it fails; flagged records are kept.
counts_file <- file.path(dirname(input_paths$harmonised_dataset_file), "harmonisation_counts.csv")
harmonisation_counts <- if (file.exists(counts_file)) read_as_text(counts_file) else NULL
count_of <- function(quantity) {
  if (is.null(harmonisation_counts)) return(NA_real_)
  as_number(harmonisation_counts$records[harmonisation_counts$quantity == quantity])[1]
}
records_read <- count_of("Tree records read from the contributor files")
if (!isTRUE(count_of("Records in the harmonised dataset") == number_of_records)) {
  warning("harmonisation_counts.csv does not match the harmonised dataset; run 1_Harmonise_tree_data.R again.",
          call. = FALSE)
  records_read <- NA_real_
}

issue_records <- function(steps, severities) {
  issues <- current_issues()
  unique(na.omit(issues$record_number[issues$step %in% steps & issues$severity %in% severities]))
}
record_numbers <- seq_len(number_of_records)

after_compilation <- !empty_record
after_coordinates <- after_compilation & !removed_coordinates
after_boundary    <- after_coordinates & !removed_outside
after_plausible   <- after_boundary & !removed_implausible
after_tree        <- after_plausible & !removed_not_tree
after_sensitive   <- after_tree & !removed_sensitive
after_duplicates  <- keep_record
confirm(identical(after_sensitive, passed_checks), "the data quality stages do not match the checks applied.")
confirm(sum(after_duplicates) == nrow(public_dataset), "the data quality table does not match the public file.")

flagged_coordinates <- after_coordinates & record_numbers %in% issue_records("coordinates", "warning")
flagged_boundary    <- after_boundary & record_numbers %in% issue_records("study region", c("warning", "note"))
flagged_measurement <- after_plausible &
  record_numbers %in% c(issue_records(c("measurements", "multiple stems"), "warning"),
                        issue_records("elephant damage", c("warning", "error")))
flagged_duplicates  <- after_duplicates & record_numbers %in% shared_row_position_records
flagged_taxonomy    <- after_duplicates & is_filled(recorded_species) & !is_filled(working_data$accepted_species_name)

data_quality <- tibble(
  `Validation stage` = c("Initial data compilation", "Coordinate completeness and precision",
                         "Geographic boundary checks", "Measurement plausibility", "Tree observation present",
                         "Sensitive species", "Duplicate screening", "Taxonomic harmonisation",
                         "Final public dataset"),
  `Records before` = c(records_read, sum(after_compilation), sum(after_coordinates), sum(after_boundary),
                       sum(after_plausible), sum(after_tree), sum(after_sensitive), sum(after_duplicates),
                       nrow(public_dataset)),
  Removed = c(records_read - sum(after_compilation), sum(removed_coordinates), sum(removed_outside),
              sum(removed_implausible), sum(removed_not_tree), sum(removed_sensitive),
              sum(after_sensitive & !after_duplicates), 0, NA),
  `Flagged (retained)` = c(NA, sum(flagged_coordinates), sum(flagged_boundary), sum(flagged_measurement), 0, 0,
                           sum(flagged_duplicates), sum(flagged_taxonomy), NA),
  `Records after` = c(sum(after_compilation), sum(after_coordinates), sum(after_boundary),
                      sum(after_plausible), sum(after_tree), sum(after_sensitive), sum(after_duplicates),
                      sum(after_duplicates), nrow(public_dataset))
)

data_quality_text <- data_quality %>%
  mutate(across(-`Validation stage`, ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), "\u2014", format(.x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))))

data_quality_footnote <- paste0(
  "Records after = records before \u2212 records removed. Each removed record is counted once, at the first ",
  "stage it fails. Flagged (retained): records kept in the dataset but marked for review. ",
  "Initial data compilation: tree records read from ", n_distinct(harmonised_data$source_file),
  " contributor files, less test submissions, dead trees, records of one tree merged across sheets, ",
  "identical records and records without values. Coordinate completeness and precision: records without a ",
  "valid coordinate pair, or recorded with fewer than ", minimum_recorded_decimal_places, " decimal places. ",
  "Geographic boundary checks: records more than ", coastal_tolerance_km, " km from mainland Africa were removed; ",
  "positions at sea within ", coastal_tolerance_km, " km of the coast were assigned the nearest country and flagged. ",
  "Measurement plausibility: records with a stem, height or crown value beyond error limits were removed; ",
  "values above warning limits, stem-count conflicts and elephant damage reported more than ",
  elephant_range_buffer_km, " km from the IUCN elephant ranges (value left empty) were flagged. ",
  "Tree observation present: records with no attribute of a tree and no species recorded by the observer, ",
  "and GPS track and route points, were removed. Sensitive species: records of ",
  paste(sensitive_species, collapse = ", "), " were removed with their photographs. ",
  "Duplicate screening: exact duplicates; the same tree on one date; every record at a position shared by ",
  "different trees in one file; the same position, date and tree type in different files; and near-duplicates ",
  "within ", near_duplicate_metres, " m with circumferences within ", 100 * near_duplicate_circumference_tolerance,
  "%. The most complete record was kept, except at copied positions. ",
  "Taxonomic harmonisation: records whose recorded species name had no exact species-level match in World Flora ",
  "Online; no records are removed.")

# The table is saved as an editable Word document in the style of Scientific
# Data.
save_word_table(data_quality_text, data_quality_table_number, "Records removed and flagged at each processing stage.",
                data_quality_footnote, column_widths = c(2.4, 0.95, 0.95, 0.95, 0.95),
                right_aligned_columns = 2:5,
                path = file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "table_data_quality.docx"))
write_excel_csv(data_quality, file.path(input_paths$results_folder, "table_data_quality.csv"), na = "")
```

# Outputs and reproducibility

The following files were written to the results folder:

-   **table_data_quality.docx** (and .csv): records entering and leaving each validation stage (@tbl-data-quality), as an editable Word table.
-   **public_data/`r input_paths$public_file_name`**: the public dataset (`r format(nrow(public_dataset), big.mark = ",")` records, `r ncol(public_dataset)` columns).
-   **manuscript_numbers.csv** and **manuscript_table_records_by_file.csv**: the record counts quoted in the Data Descriptor, computed from the public file.
-   **qaqc_removals_by_rule.csv**: the number of records removed by each rule (@tbl-removals-by-rule).
-   **elephant_range_sources.csv**: for each elephant species, the IUCN range file read, the presence codes kept, the number of polygons and the IUCN compilation year and citation, for citing the range data (internal use only; the range data are never deposited).
-   **tree_evidence_review.csv** and **records_without_tree_evidence.csv**: by source file, the records that reached the tree-observation check without a stem measurement and whether each was kept or removed, and every removed record with the values it holds (internal use only), for checking that no real tree was removed.
-   **photographs_for_public/**: the photographs of the public records, named by `record_id`; the folder is emptied at the start of each run.
-   **qaqc_issues.csv**: every issue found, with the original value and the action taken (internal use only; it may contain personal data).
-   **qaqc_record_flags.csv**: for each public record (by `record_id`), the QA/QC flags, the WFO taxonomy (of which only `accepted_species_name` is published) and the source columns (internal use only).
-   **qaqc_variable_summary.csv** and **table_variable_summary.docx**: the description, unit and completeness of each public variable (@tbl-completeness), the second as an editable Word table.
-   **qaqc_corrections_applied.csv**: every value changed by a correction rule (observer names, comments, rounding of elevation), with the original and corrected values, the rule applied and the `record_id` (internal use only).
-   **comment_spelling_review.csv**: words in comments not recognised by the spelling checker, with suggested corrections, for review (internal use only).
-   **observer_name_review.csv**: every person named, in alphabetical order, and the number of records (internal use only).
-   **species_name_review.csv**: species names without a species-level match, for correction (if any).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-inputs

input_files <- c(input_paths$harmonised_dataset_file, input_paths$dictionary_file,
                 input_paths$species_corrections_file, input_paths$name_corrections_file,
                 input_paths$comment_corrections_file)
input_files <- input_files[is_filled(input_files) & file.exists(input_files)]
knitr::kable(tibble(File = basename(input_files), `MD5 checksum` = unname(tools::md5sum(input_files))),
             format = "pipe")
```

This report was produced with `r R.version.string`, using sf `r packageVersion("sf")`, rnaturalearth `r packageVersion("rnaturalearth")`, `r if (requireNamespace("WorldFlora", quietly = TRUE)) paste("WorldFlora", packageVersion("WorldFlora"), "and") else ""` dplyr `r packageVersion("dplyr")`.
